change_summary: Produced an early post-entry SPY-relative underperformance bad-trade/tail-loss taxonomy without changing strategy behavior.
hypothesis: Accepted-stack bad trades may concentrate in an early post-entry SPY-relative underperformance family, where positions lose replacement value shortly after entry; measuring this single family can quantify tail-loss contribution and winner collateral without adding filters or strategy logic.
notes: Artifact shows 10/62 accepted-stack trades in the family; all 10 were losers, contributing $7,807.38 or 35.05% of all loss dollars and 54.46% of worst-five tail-loss dollars. Same-notional SPY replacement for those bad trades would have improved value by $8,795.34, with zero observed winner collateral and zero same-day accepted-winner replacement PnL. Observed-only; any future fix needs an ex-ante production-visible proxy, not this future-return label.
